580	// malformedSessionCRDTPath reports whether p targets the session-scoped CRDT
581	// namespace but is not at one of its three exact locations:
582	//
583	//	POST /v1/sessions/{sessionId}/documents/{documentId}/crdt/ops
584	//	GET  /v1/sessions/{sessionId}/documents/{documentId}/crdt/state
585	//	GET  /v1/sessions/{sessionId}/documents/{documentId}/crdt/state/subscribe
586	//
587	// a missing "ops"/"state"/"subscribe" segment, an extra segment, or a "crdt"
588	// segment in the keyword position (immediately past the document identifier)
589	// short of one of the registered shapes. ServeMux would answer those with a
590	// plain-text 404/405; every failure of these endpoints must be a JSON 400
591	// instead. Empty segments are already rejected by the guard itself.
592	//
593	// "crdt" is treated as the endpoint keyword only in the fourth segment (index
594	// 3, right after the document identifier); a session or document identifier
595	// literally named "crdt" occupies an identifier position (index 0 or 2) and
596	// keeps its ordinary routes.
597	func malformedSessionCRDTPath(p string) bool {
598		rest, ok := strings.CutPrefix(p, "/v1/sessions/")
599		if !ok {
600			return false
601		}
602		segs := strings.Split(rest, "/")
603		if len(segs) < 4 || segs[1] != "documents" || segs[3] != "crdt" {
604			return false
605		}
606		// Keyword position reached. The batch commit and the state read are both
607		// exactly {sessionId}/documents/{documentId}/crdt/{ops,state}; the
608		// subscription adds one trailing "subscribe" segment.
609		validOps := len(segs) == 5 &&
610			segs[0] != "" &&
611			segs[2] != "" &&
612			segs[4] == "ops"
613		validState := len(segs) == 5 &&
614			segs[0] != "" &&
615			segs[2] != "" &&
616			segs[4] == "state"
617		validSubscribe := len(segs) == 6 &&
618			segs[0] != "" &&
619			segs[2] != "" &&
620			segs[4] == "state" &&
621			segs[5] == "subscribe"
622		return !(validOps || validState || validSubscribe)
623	}

635	// decodeJSONBody enforces the strict POST contract shared by every JSON
636	// endpoint: Content-Type must be application/json, the body is capped at
637	// maxBatchBytes, it must contain exactly one JSON value, and no trailing data
638	// may follow it. Any violation writes a 400 JSON error and returns false; the
639	// caller returns immediately, so no handler reaches the store with malformed
640	// input and rejected requests write nothing.
641	func decodeJSONBody(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request, dst any) bool {
642		mediaType, _, err := mime.ParseMediaType(r.Header.Get("Content-Type"))
643		if err != nil || mediaType != "application/json" {
644			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "Content-Type must be application/json")
645			return false
646		}
647	
648		r.Body = http.MaxBytesReader(w, r.Body, maxBatchBytes)
649		dec := json.NewDecoder(r.Body)
650		if err := dec.Decode(dst); err != nil {
651			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid JSON body: "+err.Error())
652			return false
653		}
654		// Reject trailing data after the JSON value.
655		if err := dec.Decode(&struct{}{}); !errors.Is(err, io.EOF) {
656			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid JSON body: unexpected trailing content")
657			return false
658		}
659		return true
660	}

681	// handleDeregisterDevice removes a registered device and everything it owns
682	// in one serialized, synchronously committed cascade. The path device id is
683	// the caller's only identity and the call carries no body: a present body is
684	// accepted without being read (deregistration never interprets one), but the
685	// path must be exact. Success answers a single JSON line naming the device id
686	// and the deletion marker and nothing else. A device that was never
687	// registered, or one that is deregistered a second time, is a 404 JSON error
688	// and writes nothing; concurrent calls take effect at most once.
689	func handleDeregisterDevice(s *app.App, w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
690		deviceID := r.PathValue("deviceId") // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
691	
692		if err := s.DeregisterDevice(deviceID); err != nil {
693			if errors.Is(err, store.ErrDeviceNotFound) {
694				writeError(w, http.StatusNotFound, "device not found")
695				return
696			}
697			writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to deregister device")
698			return
699		}
700	
701		writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{"deviceId": deviceID, "deleted": true})
702	}

749	func handlePostChanges(s *app.App, w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
750		documentID := r.PathValue("documentID") // route pattern guarantees non-empty
751	
752		mediaType, _, err := mime.ParseMediaType(r.Header.Get("Content-Type"))
753		if err != nil || mediaType != "application/json" {
754			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "Content-Type must be application/json")
755			return
756		}
757	
758		r.Body = http.MaxBytesReader(w, r.Body, maxBatchBytes)
759		var req postRequest
760		dec := json.NewDecoder(r.Body)
761		if err := dec.Decode(&req); err != nil {
762			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid JSON body: "+err.Error())
763			return
764		}
765		// Reject trailing data after the JSON object.
766		if err := dec.Decode(&struct{}{}); !errors.Is(err, io.EOF) {
767			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid JSON body: unexpected trailing content")
768			return
769		}
770	
771		if req.DeviceID == "" {
772			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "deviceId must be a non-empty string")
773			return
774		}
775		if len(req.Changes) == 0 {
776			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "changes must be a non-empty array")
777			return
778		}
779	
780		changes := make([]events.Change, len(req.Changes))
781		seen := make(map[string]struct{}, len(req.Changes))
782		for i, c := range req.Changes {
783			if c.ID == "" {
784				writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "each change must have a non-empty string id")
785				return
786			}
787			if len(c.Payload) == 0 {
788				writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "each change must carry a JSON payload")
789				return
790			}
791			if _, dup := seen[c.ID]; dup {
792				writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "duplicate change id within batch: "+c.ID)
793				return
794			}
795			seen[c.ID] = struct{}{}
796			changes[i] = events.Change{ID: c.ID, DeviceID: req.DeviceID, Payload: c.Payload}
797		}
798	
799		results, err := s.PostChanges(documentID, changes)
800		if err != nil {
801			var conflict *events.ErrConflict
802			if errors.As(err, &conflict) {
803				writeError(w, http.StatusConflict, "change id already exists with different deviceId or payload: "+conflict.ID)
804				return
805			}
806			writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to commit changes")
807			return
808		}
809	
810		writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{"results": results})
811	}

813	func handleMergeChange(s *app.App, w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
814		documentID := r.PathValue("documentID") // route pattern guarantees non-empty
815	
816		mediaType, _, err := mime.ParseMediaType(r.Header.Get("Content-Type"))
817		if err != nil || mediaType != "application/json" {
818			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "Content-Type must be application/json")
819			return
820		}
821	
822		r.Body = http.MaxBytesReader(w, r.Body, maxBatchBytes)
823		var req mergeRequest
824		dec := json.NewDecoder(r.Body)
825		if err := dec.Decode(&req); err != nil {
826			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid JSON body: "+err.Error())
827			return
828		}
829		if err := dec.Decode(&struct{}{}); !errors.Is(err, io.EOF) {
830			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid JSON body: unexpected trailing content")
831			return
832		}
833	
834		if req.DeviceID == "" {
835			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "deviceId must be a non-empty string")
836			return
837		}
838		// baseCursor must be present and a non-negative integer (no fractions,
839		// strings, booleans or null).
840		if len(req.BaseCursor) == 0 {
841			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "baseCursor must be a non-negative integer")
842			return
843		}
844		baseCursor, ok := parseNonNegativeInt(req.BaseCursor)
845		if !ok {
846			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "baseCursor must be a non-negative integer")
847			return
848		}
849		if req.Change == nil {
850			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "change must be an object")
851			return
852		}
853		if req.Change.ID == "" {
854			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "change.id must be a non-empty string")
855			return
856		}
857		if len(req.Change.Payload) == 0 || !isJSONObject(req.Change.Payload) {
858			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "change.payload must be a JSON object")
859			return
860		}
861	
862		result, err := s.MergeChange(documentID, baseCursor, events.Change{
863			ID:       req.Change.ID,
864			DeviceID: req.DeviceID,
865			Payload:  req.Change.Payload,
866		})
867		if err != nil {
868			var conflict *events.ErrConflict
869			switch {
870			case errors.Is(err, events.ErrStaleCursor):
871				writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "baseCursor is unknown or greater than the current cursor")
872				return
873			case errors.Is(err, events.ErrCompactedBase):
874				writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "baseCursor is below the compaction boundary")
875				return
876			case errors.As(err, &conflict):
877				writeError(w, http.StatusConflict, "merge conflicts with existing changes: "+conflict.ID)
878				return
879			default:
880				writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to merge change")
881				return
882			}
883		}
884	
885		writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, result)

1065	// parseCursorPath reports whether raw is a decimal non-negative integer and
1066	// returns its value. Signs, fractions and other adornments are rejected.
1067	func parseCursorPath(raw string) (int64, bool) {
1068		if raw == "" {
1069			return 0, false
1070		}
1071		for _, c := range raw {
1072			if c < '0' || c > '9' {
1073				return 0, false
1074			}
1075		}
1076		n, err := strconv.ParseInt(raw, 10, 64)
1077		if err != nil {
1078			return 0, false
1079		}
1080		return n, true
1081	}

1083	// parseNonNegativeInt reports whether raw is a JSON integer >= 0. Floats,// strings, booleans, null and negative numbers are rejected.
1084	func parseNonNegativeInt(raw json.RawMessage) (int64, bool) {
1085		var n int64
1086		if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &n); err != nil || n < 0 {
1087			return 0, false
1088		}
1089		// Guard against values like 1.0 that Unmarshal into int64 on some inputs;
1090		// require the literal to contain no fraction or exponent.
1091		trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(string(raw))
1092		if trimmed == "" || trimmed[0] == '-' {
1093			return 0, false
1094		}
1095		for _, c := range trimmed {
1096			if c < '0' || c > '9' {
1097				return 0, false
1098			}
1099		}
1100		return n, true
1101	}

1104	// strings, booleans, null and negative numbers are rejected.
1105	func parsePositiveInt(raw json.RawMessage) (int64, bool) {
1106		n, ok := parseNonNegativeInt(raw)

1109		}
1110		return n, true
1111	}

1119		}

1205	// handleSessionPostChanges is the session-scoped batch commit over the same
1206	// change collection the session reads page:
1207	//
1208	//	POST /v1/sessions/{sessionId}/documents/{documentId}/changes
1209	//
1210	// The request body carries only the changes array — the calling device is the
1211	// session's owning device, resolved with the same identity rule as the
1212	// session reads, exports and subscriptions; no new credential is introduced
1213	// and no device id travels in the body. Per-element semantics and the success
1214	// body are byte-identical to the document-level commit: results arrive in
1215	// request order, each naming its id, whether it was created and the cursor it
1216	// was assigned. The checks run in the fixed order request shape (400),
1217	// session existence (404), document permission (403) — the permission verdict
1218	// is taken inside the commit transaction, so a revoked device writes nothing —
1219	// and a payload/device mismatch against an existing id is a 409 reporting the
1220	// conflicting id. Every rejection leaves the log untouched.
1221	func handleSessionPostChanges(s *app.App, w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
1222		sessionID := r.PathValue("sessionId")   // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
1223		documentID := r.PathValue("documentId") // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
1224	
1225		var req sessionPostRequest
1226		if !decodeJSONBody(w, r, &req) {
1227			return
1228		}
1229		if len(req.Changes) == 0 {
1230			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "changes must be a non-empty array")
1231			return
1232		}
1233	
1234		changes := make([]events.Change, len(req.Changes))
1235		seen := make(map[string]struct{}, len(req.Changes))
1236		for i, c := range req.Changes {
1237			if c.ID == "" {
1238				writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "each change must have a non-empty string id")
1239				return
1240			}
1241			if len(c.Payload) == 0 {
1242				writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "each change must carry a JSON payload")
1243				return
1244			}
1245			if _, dup := seen[c.ID]; dup {
1246				writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "duplicate change id within batch: "+c.ID)
1247				return
1248			}
1249			seen[c.ID] = struct{}{}
1250			changes[i] = events.Change{ID: c.ID, Payload: c.Payload}
1251		}
1252	
1253		// Request shape is settled; only now does the session lookup run, so a
1254		// malformed batch against an unknown session is still a 400.
1255		deviceID, err := s.SessionDevice(sessionID)
1256		if err != nil {
1257			if errors.Is(err, store.ErrSessionNotFound) {
1258				writeError(w, http.StatusNotFound, "session not found")
1259				return
1260			}
1261			writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to look up session")
1262			return
1263		}
1264		for i := range changes {
1265			changes[i].DeviceID = deviceID
1266		}
1267	
1268		results, err := s.PostSessionChanges(documentID, changes)
1269		if err != nil {
1270			var conflict *events.ErrConflict
1271			switch {
1272			case errors.Is(err, store.ErrDeviceNotFound):
1273				// The session's device was deregistered between the lookup and
1274				// the commit; its cascade removed the session too, so the
1275				// identity the caller used no longer exists.
1276				writeError(w, http.StatusNotFound, "session not found")
1277			case errors.Is(err, store.ErrPermissionDenied):
1278				writeError(w, http.StatusForbidden, "device permission for this document has been revoked")
1279			case errors.As(err, &conflict):
1280				writeJSON(w, http.StatusConflict, map[string]string{
1281					"error":      "change id already exists with different deviceId or payload",
1282					"conflictId": conflict.ID,
1283				})
1284			default:
1285				writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to commit changes")
1286			}
1287			return
1288		}

1290		writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{"results": results})

1446		if len(req.Change.Payload) == 0 || !isJSONObject(req.Change.Payload) {
1447			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "change.payload must be a JSON object")
1448			return
1449		}
1450	
1451		// Request shape is settled; only now does the session lookup run, so a
1452		// malformed merge against an unknown session is still a 400.
1453		deviceID, err := s.SessionDevice(sessionID)
1454		if err != nil {
1455			if errors.Is(err, store.ErrSessionNotFound) {
1456				writeError(w, http.StatusNotFound, "session not found")
1457				return
1458			}
1459			writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to look up session")
1460			return
1461		}
1462	
1463		result, err := s.MergeSessionChange(documentID, baseCursor, events.Change{
1464			ID:       req.Change.ID,
1465			DeviceID: deviceID,
1466			Payload:  req.Change.Payload,
1467		})
1468		if err != nil {
1469			var conflict *events.ErrConflict
1470			switch {
1471			case errors.Is(err, store.ErrDeviceNotFound):
1472				// The session's device was deregistered between the lookup and the
1473				// merge; its cascade removed the session too, so the identity the
1474				// caller used no longer exists.
1475				writeError(w, http.StatusNotFound, "session not found")
1476			case errors.Is(err, store.ErrPermissionDenied):
1477				writeError(w, http.StatusForbidden, "device permission for this document has been revoked")
1478			case errors.Is(err, events.ErrStaleCursor):
1479				writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "baseCursor is unknown or greater than the current cursor")
1480			case errors.Is(err, events.ErrCompactedBase):
1481				writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "baseCursor is below the compaction boundary")
1482			case errors.As(err, &conflict):
1483				writeError(w, http.StatusConflict, "merge conflicts with existing changes: "+conflict.ID)
1484			default:
1485				writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to merge change")
1486			}
1487			return
1488		}
1489	
1490		writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, result)
1491	}
1492	
1493	// parseChangesQuery parses the shared after/limit pagination parameters,
1494	// writing the documented 400 on an illegal value. It is shared by the
1495	// document-scoped and session-scoped change listings so their query semantics
1496	// cannot drift apart.
1497	func parseChangesQuery(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) (after, limit int64, ok bool) {
1498		q := r.URL.Query()
1499	
1500		after = 0
1501		if raw := q.Get("after"); raw != "" {
1502			v, err := strconv.ParseInt(raw, 10, 64)
1503			if err != nil || v < 0 {
1504				writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "after must be a non-negative integer")
1505				return 0, 0, false
1506			}
1507			after = v
1508		}
1509	
1510		limit = defaultListLimit
1511		if raw := q.Get("limit"); raw != "" {
1512			v, err := strconv.ParseInt(raw, 10, 64)
1513			if err != nil || v < 1 || v > maxListLimit {
1514				writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "limit must be an integer between 1 and 1000")
1515				return 0, 0, false
1516			}
1517			limit = v
1518		}
1519	
1520		return after, limit, true
1521	}
1522	
1523	// writeChangesPage renders a change listing page in the shared response shape.
1524	func writeChangesPage(w http.ResponseWriter, changes []events.ListedChange, nextCursor int64) {
1525		writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{
1526			"changes":    changes,
1527			"nextCursor": nextCursor,
1528		})
1529	}
1530	
1531	// parsePollWaitMs parses the long-poll waitMs query parameter, writing the
1532	// documented 400 on an illegal value. It accepts an integer in 0..30000
1533	// milliseconds and defaults to 0 when the parameter is absent; a value outside
1534	// the range, a fraction, an exponent or any non-numeric value is rejected. It
1535	// is shared by the document-scoped and session-scoped long polls so their wait
1536	// semantics cannot drift apart.
1537	func parsePollWaitMs(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) (int64, bool) {
1538		var waitMs int64
1539		if raw := r.URL.Query().Get("waitMs"); raw != "" {
1540			v, err := strconv.ParseInt(raw, 10, 64)
1541			if err != nil || v < 0 || v > maxPollWaitMillis {
1542				writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "waitMs must be an integer between 0 and 30000")
1543				return 0, false
1544			}
1545			waitMs = v
1546		}
1547		return waitMs, true
1548	}
1549	
1550	// writePollPage renders a long-poll result in the shared response shape: the
1551	// ordinary page plus a timedOut flag, with the top-level keys in the fixed
1552	// changes, nextCursor, timedOut order.
1553	func writePollPage(w http.ResponseWriter, changes []events.ListedChange, nextCursor int64, timedOut bool) {
1554		writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{
1555			"changes":    changes,
1556			"nextCursor": nextCursor,
1557			"timedOut":   timedOut,
1558		})
1559	}
1560	
1561	func writeJSON(w http.ResponseWriter, status int, v any) {
1562		w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
1563		w.WriteHeader(status)
1564		_ = json.NewEncoder(w).Encode(v)
1565	}
1566	
1567	func writeError(w http.ResponseWriter, status int, message string) {
1568		writeJSON(w, status, map[string]string{"error": message})
1569	}
1570	
1571	// handlePollChanges is the long-polling entry over the change log.
1572	//
1573	// Query params share the existing change-read constraints: after is a
1574	// non-negative cursor (default 0) and limit is 1..1000 (default 100); waitMs
1575	// is 0..30000 (default 0). Rows already past after return immediately; a known
1576	// document caught up to after parks until the first new commit or the wait
1577	// deadline; an unknown document returns an empty page with cursor 0 at once.
1578	// The response shape is the ordinary page plus a timedOut flag; a deadline
1579	// expiry echoes the caller's cursor and never advances it. A client
1580	// disconnect simply stops the wait and writes nothing.
1581	func handlePollChanges(s *app.App, w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
1582		documentID := r.PathValue("documentID") // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
1583	
1584		after, limit, ok := parseChangesQuery(w, r)
1585		if !ok {
1586			return
1587		}
1588		waitMs, ok := parsePollWaitMs(w, r)
1589		if !ok {
1590			return
1591		}
1592	
1593		changes, nextCursor, timedOut, err := s.WaitForChanges(
1594			r.Context(), documentID, after, limit, time.Duration(waitMs)*time.Millisecond,
1595		)
1596		switch {
1597		case errors.Is(err, events.ErrStoreClosing):
1598			writeError(w, http.StatusServiceUnavailable, "service is shutting down")
1599			return
1600		case errors.Is(err, context.Canceled), errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded):
1601			// The client went away (or, with waitMs bounded, its deadline lapsed
1602			// at the transport): nothing more to write and nothing was stored.
1603			return
1604		case err != nil:
1605			writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to poll changes")
1606			return
1607		}
1608	
1609		writePollPage(w, changes, nextCursor, timedOut)
1610	}
1611	
1612	// handleSessionPollChanges is the session-scoped long-poll continuation over
1613	// the same change collection the session reads page:
1614	//
1615	//	GET /v1/sessions/{sessionId}/documents/{documentId}/changes/poll
1616	//
1617	// The request is a GET with no body; the calling device is the session's
1618	// owning device resolved with the same identity rule as the session reads,
1619	// exports, commits and subscriptions. Query parameters and the success body are
1620	// identical to GET /v1/documents/{documentID}/changes/poll — after (default 0),
1621	// limit (default 100, 1..1000) and waitMs (default 0, 0..30000), answered with
1622	// changes, nextCursor and timedOut in that order, rows ascending by cursor.
1623	//
1624	// Rows already past after return immediately with timedOut=false; a known
1625	// document caught up to after parks until the first commit through any write
1626	// path (session batch commit, document commit, merge, restore, replay) or the
1627	// wait deadline; an unknown document returns an empty page with cursor 0 at
1628	// once and never parks. A deadline expiry returns the empty page, echoes the
1629	// caller's after and sets timedOut=true without advancing the cursor. Checks
1630	// run in the fixed order request shape and parameters (400), session
1631	// existence (404), document permission (403); a rejected request exposes no
1632	// change content. A client disconnect simply cancels the wait and writes
1633	// nothing; while the service is shutting down the parked request answers a
1634	// JSON 503.
1635	func handleSessionPollChanges(s *app.App, w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
1636		sessionID := r.PathValue("sessionId")   // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
1637		documentID := r.PathValue("documentId") // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
1638	
1639		// Parameter shape precedes the session lookup, matching the session paged
1640		// read's ordering: a malformed after/limit/waitMs against an unknown
1641		// session is still a 400.
1642		after, limit, ok := parseChangesQuery(w, r)
1643		if !ok {
1644			return
1645		}
1646		waitMs, ok := parsePollWaitMs(w, r)
1647		if !ok {
1648			return
1649		}
1650	
1651		deviceID, err := s.SessionDevice(sessionID)
1652		if err != nil {
1653			if errors.Is(err, store.ErrSessionNotFound) {
1654				writeError(w, http.StatusNotFound, "session not found")
1655				return
1656			}
1657			writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to look up session")
1658			return
1659		}
1660	
1661		authorized, err := s.DocumentAuthorized(documentID, deviceID)
1662		if err != nil {
1663			writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to look up permission")
1664			return
1665		}
1666		if !authorized {
1667			writeError(w, http.StatusForbidden, "device permission for this document has been revoked")
1668			return
1669		}
1670	
1671		changes, nextCursor, timedOut, err := s.WaitForChanges(
1672			r.Context(), documentID, after, limit, time.Duration(waitMs)*time.Millisecond,
1673		)
1674		switch {
1675		case errors.Is(err, events.ErrStoreClosing):
1676			writeError(w, http.StatusServiceUnavailable, "service is shutting down")
1677			return
1678		case errors.Is(err, context.Canceled), errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded):
1679			// The client went away (or, with waitMs bounded, its deadline lapsed
1680			// at the transport): nothing more to write and nothing was stored.
1681			return
1682		case err != nil:
1683			writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to poll changes")
1684			return
1685		}
1686	
1687		writePollPage(w, changes, nextCursor, timedOut)
1688	}
1689	
1690	// handleReplay retries an offline batch against the existing change log. The
1691	// request and per-element semantics mirror POST .../changes — strict
1692	// application/json body, non-empty ids, no in-batch duplicates, idempotent only
1693	// when deviceId and decoded payload match, otherwise 409 reporting the
1694	// conflicting id — with the registration/permission layer enforced first:
1695	// 404 for an unregistered device and 403 for a revoked one, neither exposing
1696	// change content. The whole batch commits in one serialized transaction that
1697	// shares the document's contiguous cursor space with ordinary commits.
1698	func handleReplay(s *app.App, w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
1699		documentID := r.PathValue("documentID") // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
1700	
1701		var req replayRequest
1702		if !decodeJSONBody(w, r, &req) {
1703			return
1704		}
1705		if req.DeviceID == "" {
1706			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "deviceId must be a non-empty string")
1707			return
1708		}
1709		if req.Operations == nil {
1710			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "operations must be a non-empty array")
1711			return
1712		}
1713		if len(req.Operations) == 0 {
1714			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "operations must be a non-empty array")
1715			return
1716		}
1717	
1718		changes := make([]events.Change, len(req.Operations))
1719		seen := make(map[string]struct{}, len(req.Operations))
1720		for i, op := range req.Operations {
1721			if op.ID == "" {
1722				writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "each operation must have a non-empty string id")
1723				return
1724			}
1725			if len(op.Payload) == 0 {
1726				writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "each operation must carry a JSON payload")
1727				return
1728			}
1729			if _, dup := seen[op.ID]; dup {
1730				writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "duplicate operation id within batch: "+op.ID)
1731				return
1732			}
1733			seen[op.ID] = struct{}{}
1734			changes[i] = events.Change{ID: op.ID, DeviceID: req.DeviceID, Payload: op.Payload}
1735		}
1736	
1737		results, err := s.ReplayChanges(documentID, changes)
1738		if err != nil {
1739			var conflict *events.ErrConflict
1740			switch {
1741			case errors.Is(err, store.ErrDeviceNotFound):
1742				writeError(w, http.StatusNotFound, "device not found")
1743			case errors.Is(err, store.ErrPermissionDenied):
1744				writeError(w, http.StatusForbidden, "device permission for this document has been revoked")
1745			case errors.As(err, &conflict):
1746				writeJSON(w, http.StatusConflict, map[string]string{
1747					"error":      "operation id already exists with different deviceId or payload",
1748					"conflictId": conflict.ID,
1749				})
1750			default:
1751				writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to replay operations")
1752			}
1753			return
1754		}
1755	
1756		writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{"results": results})
1757	}

1	// Package app is the composition root: it opens the one shared database and
2	// constructs the three independently reusable internal services — the change
3	// event service, the permission service and the CRDT state service — wiring
4	// them together only through their internal interfaces.
5	//
6	// The services share one SQLite connection (the kernel opens a single
7	// pooled connection with immediate transactions), so a change commit, a CRDT
8	// submission or compaction, and a permission change are serialized on the
9	// same connection and leave no half-written batch. The change event and CRDT
10	// services take their registration-and-authorization verdict from the
11	// permission service inside their own transactions (events.Gate / crdt.Gate),
12	// and the permission service fans a committed revoke out to their
13	// subscription registries through authz.RevokeSink. No service reaches into
14	// another service's tables or fields.
15	//
16	// App is the single object the entry and HTTP layers use. It promotes each
17	// service's input/output boundary as its methods while hiding the wiring; it
18	// adds no authentication and exposes no endpoint of its own.
19	package app
20	
21	import (
22		"context"
23		"encoding/json"
24		"time"
25	
26		"github.com/alicegogogogogo/local-first-sync-service/internal/authz"
27		"github.com/alicegogogogogo/local-first-sync-service/internal/crdt"
28		"github.com/alicegogogogogo/local-first-sync-service/internal/events"
29		"github.com/alicegogogogogo/local-first-sync-service/internal/store"
30	)
31	
32	// App composes the durable kernel and the three internal services over one
33	// shared database connection.
34	type App struct {
35		*store.Store
36	
37		events *events.Service
38		crdt   *crdt.Service
39	
40		// Authz is the permission service. It is exposed so the HTTP layer can
41		// grant/revoke and read authorization directly; the other services reach
42		// it through their gates rather than this field.
43		Authz *authz.Service
44	}
45	
46	// Open opens (creating if needed) the SQLite database at path and constructs
47	// every internal service over it. The empty path opens a private in-memory
48	// database useful for tests. A construction failure closes the kernel and
49	// leaves nothing behind.
50	func Open(path string) (*App, error) {
51		kernel, err := store.Open(path)
52		if err != nil {
53			return nil, err
54		}
55	
56		// The permission service is built first: its gate is a constructor
57		// dependency of the change event and CRDT services.
58		permissions, err := authz.New(kernel)
59		if err != nil {
60			_ = kernel.Close()
61			return nil, err
62		}
63		eventService, err := events.New(kernel, permissions)
64		if err != nil {
65			_ = kernel.Close()
66			return nil, err
67		}
68		crdtService, err := crdt.New(kernel, permissions)
69		if err != nil {
70			_ = kernel.Close()
71			return nil, err
72		}
73	
74		// A committed revoke ends the affected live subscriptions in both
75		// push channels. The dependency is an interface, registered once here, so
76		// the permission service never names either subscriber concretely.
77		permissions.AddRevokeSink(eventsRevokeSink{eventService})
78		permissions.AddRevokeSink(crdtService)
79	
80		return &App{
81			Store:  kernel,
82			events: eventService,
83			crdt:   crdtService,
84			Authz:  permissions,
85		}, nil
86	}
87	
88	// eventsRevokeSink adapts the change event service's revoke hook to the
89	// permission service's RevokeSink interface.
90	type eventsRevokeSink struct{ e *events.Service }
91	
92	func (s eventsRevokeSink) PermissionRevoked(documentID, deviceID string) {
93		s.e.SignalRevoked(documentID, deviceID)
94	}
95	
96	// Events returns the change event service.
97	func (a *App) Events() *events.Service { return a.events }
98	
99	// CRDT returns the CRDT state service.
100	func (a *App) CRDT() *crdt.Service { return a.crdt }
101	
102	// ---- Change event service boundary (promoted so the entry layer has one
103	// object; each method delegates verbatim to the events service). ----
104	
105	// InterruptWaits wakes every parked long poll and every live change-log and
106	// CRDT subscription without closing the database, so an orderly shutdown
107	// drains waiting connections (long polls answer 503; subscriptions finish
108	// with the going-away close) instead of holding the drain hostage.
109	func (a *App) InterruptWaits() {
110		a.events.InterruptWaits()
111		a.crdt.InterruptWaits()
112	}
113	
114	// Closing reports whether shutdown has begun, covering both push channels.
115	func (a *App) Closing() bool {
116		return a.events.Closing() || a.crdt.Closing()
117	}
118	
119	// Close interrupts the in-memory observers, waits for every subscription
120	// handler to unregister and then releases the shared database handle.
121	func (a *App) Close() error {
122		a.events.InterruptWaits()
123		a.crdt.InterruptWaits()
124		a.events.WaitDrained()
125		a.crdt.WaitDrained()
126		return a.Store.Close()
127	}
128	
129	// PostChanges delegates to the change event service.
130	func (a *App) PostChanges(documentID string, changes []events.Change) ([]events.Result, error) {
131		return a.events.PostChanges(documentID, changes)
132	}
133	
134	// ReplayChanges delegates to the change event service.
135	func (a *App) ReplayChanges(documentID string, changes []events.Change) ([]events.Result, error) {
136		return a.events.ReplayChanges(documentID, changes)
137	}
138	
139	// PostSessionChanges commits a batch whose device identity was resolved from
140	// a session by the HTTP layer, delegating to the change event service's
141	// gated commit: the registration/permission verdict is taken inside the same
142	// serialized transaction as the write, so a revoked device commits nothing.
143	func (a *App) PostSessionChanges(documentID string, changes []events.Change) ([]events.Result, error) {
144		return a.events.CommitAuthorized(documentID, changes)
145	}
146	
147	// ReplaySessionChanges replays an offline batch whose device identity was
148	// resolved from a session by the HTTP layer; it is the session counterpart
149	// to ReplayChanges and commits through the same gated transaction the
150	// session-scoped batch commit uses, so the two paths cannot drift.
151	func (a *App) ReplaySessionChanges(documentID string, changes []events.Change) ([]events.Result, error) {
152		return a.events.CommitAuthorized(documentID, changes)
153	}
154	
155	// MergeChange delegates to the change event service.
156	func (a *App) MergeChange(documentID string, baseCursor int64, c events.Change) (events.MergeResult, error) {
157		return a.events.MergeChange(documentID, baseCursor, c)
158	}
159	
160	// MergeSessionChange merges a single change whose device identity was resolved
161	// from a session by the HTTP layer, delegating to the change event service's
162	// gated merge: the registration/permission verdict is taken inside the same
163	// serialized transaction as the merge judgment and append, so a revoked device
164	// writes nothing and a rejected request observes no change content.
165	func (a *App) MergeSessionChange(documentID string, baseCursor int64, c events.Change) (events.MergeResult, error) {
166		return a.events.MergeChangeAuthorized(documentID, baseCursor, c)
167	}
168	
169	// PutSnapshot delegates to the change event service.
170	func (a *App) PutSnapshot(documentID string, cursor int64, state json.RawMessage) (bool, error) {
171		return a.events.PutSnapshot(documentID, cursor, state)
172	}
173	
174	// GetSnapshot delegates to the change event service.
175	func (a *App) GetSnapshot(documentID string, cursor int64) (json.RawMessage, error) {
176		return a.events.GetSnapshot(documentID, cursor)
177	}
178	
179	// ExportSnapshots delegates to the change event service. A nil to means the
180	// interval has no upper bound.
181	func (a *App) ExportSnapshots(documentID string, from int64, to *int64) ([]events.ExportedSnapshot, error) {
182		return a.events.ExportSnapshots(documentID, from, to)
183	}
184	
185	// RestoreSnapshot delegates to the change event service.
186	func (a *App) RestoreSnapshot(documentID, deviceID, changeID string, snapshotCursor int64) (events.RestoreResult, error) {
187		return a.events.RestoreSnapshot(documentID, deviceID, changeID, snapshotCursor)
188	}
189	
190	// ListChanges delegates to the change event service.
191	func (a *App) ListChanges(documentID string, after, limit int64) ([]events.ListedChange, int64, error) {
192		return a.events.ListChanges(documentID, after, limit)
193	}
194	
195	// ExportChanges delegates to the change event service. A nil to means the
196	// interval has no upper bound.
197	func (a *App) ExportChanges(documentID string, from int64, to *int64) ([]events.ListedChange, error) {
198		return a.events.ExportChanges(documentID, from, to)
199	}
200	
201	// WaitForChanges delegates to the change event service.
202	func (a *App) WaitForChanges(ctx context.Context, documentID string, after, limit int64, wait time.Duration) ([]events.ListedChange, int64, bool, error) {
203		return a.events.WaitForChanges(ctx, documentID, after, limit, wait)
204	}
205	
206	// DocumentExists delegates to the change event service.
207	func (a *App) DocumentExists(documentID string) (bool, error) {
208		return a.events.DocumentExists(documentID)
209	}

211	// CompactChanges delegates to the change event service.

1	package events
2	
3	import (
4		"bytes"
5		"database/sql"
6		"encoding/json"
7		"errors"
8	
9		"github.com/alicegogogogogo/local-first-sync-service/internal/store"
10	)
11	
12	// PutSnapshot stores state as the snapshot of documentID at cursor, creating
13	// it on first use and reporting whether this call created it.
14	//
15	// Only cursors of existing changes are valid snapshot points: an unknown
16	// document, a cursor below 1 or a cursor ahead of the document's current
17	// cursor yields ErrSnapshotBase and nothing is written. The current cursor is
18	// the document's high-water mark in the never-reset cursor space — the
19	// greater of the online maximum and the compaction boundary — so a cursor
20	// whose change has been trimmed by compaction is still a valid snapshot
21	// point, even after a full trim emptied the online log. Re-posting a state
22	// that decodes equal to the stored one is idempotent (created=false); a
23	// different state is an *ErrSnapshotConflict and the stored snapshot is left
24	// unchanged. Snapshots are independent of the change log: they neither move
25	// the document's cursor nor affect merges.
26	func (s *Service) PutSnapshot(documentID string, cursor int64, state json.RawMessage) (bool, error) {
27		tx, err := s.db.Begin()
28		if err != nil {
29			return false, err
30		}
31		defer func() { _ = tx.Rollback() }()
32	
33		current, err := currentCursorTx(tx, documentID)
34		if err != nil {
35			return false, err
36		}
37		if current == 0 || cursor < 1 || cursor > current {
38			return false, ErrSnapshotBase
39		}
40	
41		var existing []byte
42		err = tx.QueryRow(
43			`SELECT state FROM snapshots WHERE document_id = ? AND cursor = ?`,
44			documentID, cursor,
45		).Scan(&existing)
46		switch {
47		case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
48			if _, err := tx.Exec(
49				`INSERT INTO snapshots (document_id, cursor, state) VALUES (?, ?, ?)`,
50				documentID, cursor, []byte(state),
51			); err != nil {
52				return false, err
53			}
54			if err := tx.Commit(); err != nil {
55				return false, err
56			}
57			return true, nil
58		case err != nil:
59			return false, err
60		default:
61			if !store.JSONEqual(existing, state) {
62				return false, &ErrSnapshotConflict{Cursor: cursor}
63			}
64			return false, nil
65		}
66	}
67	
68	// GetSnapshot returns the state stored for documentID at cursor. Any miss —
69	// unknown document, unknown cursor or absent snapshot — yields
70	// ErrSnapshotNotFound.
71	func (s *Service) GetSnapshot(documentID string, cursor int64) (json.RawMessage, error) {
72		var state []byte
73		err := s.db.QueryRow(
74			`SELECT state FROM snapshots WHERE document_id = ? AND cursor = ?`,
75			documentID, cursor,
76		).Scan(&state)
77		switch {
78		case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
79			return nil, ErrSnapshotNotFound
80		case err != nil:
81			return nil, err
82		default:
83			return json.RawMessage(state), nil
84		}
85	}
86	
87	// ExportSnapshots returns every snapshot of documentID whose cursor lies in
88	// the closed interval [from, to], in ascending cursor order. When to is nil no
89	// upper bound is applied. An unknown document, or a range without a snapshot,
90	// yields an empty list and no error: the export is a read that misses like any
91	// other. The (document_id, cursor) primary key guarantees a cursor appears at
92	// most once.
93	//
94	// The single SELECT runs as one SQLite statement over the serialized
95	// connection, so a snapshot committed concurrently is observed either with all
96	// of its row or not at all — never half of it. The read starts no
97	// transaction, writes nothing and notifies no waiters, so it cannot move a
98	// cursor or produce a change record.
99	func (s *Service) ExportSnapshots(documentID string, from int64, to *int64) ([]ExportedSnapshot, error) {
100		var (
101			rows *sql.Rows
102			err  error
103		)
104		if to == nil {
105			rows, err = s.db.Query(
106				`SELECT cursor, state FROM snapshots
107				 WHERE document_id = ? AND cursor >= ?
108				 ORDER BY cursor ASC`,
109				documentID, from,
110			)
111		} else {
112			rows, err = s.db.Query(
113				`SELECT cursor, state FROM snapshots
114				 WHERE document_id = ? AND cursor >= ? AND cursor <= ?
115				 ORDER BY cursor ASC`,
116				documentID, from, *to,
117			)
118		}
119		if err != nil {
120			return nil, err
121		}
122		defer func() { _ = rows.Close() }()
123	
124		out := make([]ExportedSnapshot, 0)
125		for rows.Next() {
126			var snap ExportedSnapshot
127			if err := rows.Scan(&snap.Cursor, &snap.State); err != nil {
128				return nil, err
129			}
130			out = append(out, snap)
131		}
132		if err := rows.Err(); err != nil {
133			return nil, err
134		}
135		return out, nil
136	}
137	
138	// RestoreSnapshot appends one ordinary change whose payload is the state of
139	// documentID's snapshot at snapshotCursor, all within a single serialized
140	// transaction.
141	//
142	//   - A snapshot miss (unknown document or a cursor without a snapshot)
143	//     returns ErrSnapshotNotFound; nothing is written.
144	//   - If changeID already belongs to a prior restore, the call is idempotent
145	//     only when deviceId, snapshotCursor and the decoded source state all
146	//     match; the first result (created=false, original cursor) is returned.
147	//   - If changeID is taken by an ordinary change, or a restore whose provenance
148	//     differs, the call returns *ErrRestoreConflict; nothing is written.
149	//
150	// Otherwise a new change is appended with the next document cursor and the
151	// restore provenance is recorded. Old rows are never modified.
152	func (s *Service) RestoreSnapshot(documentID, deviceID, changeID string, snapshotCursor int64) (RestoreResult, error) {
153		tx, err := s.db.Begin()
154		if err != nil {
155			return RestoreResult{}, err
156		}
157		defer func() { _ = tx.Rollback() }()
158	
159		// The snapshot must exist; its state is the payload to append.
160		var state []byte
161		err = tx.QueryRow(
162			`SELECT state FROM snapshots WHERE document_id = ? AND cursor = ?`,
163			documentID, snapshotCursor,
164		).Scan(&state)
165		switch {
166		case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
167			return RestoreResult{}, ErrSnapshotNotFound
168		case err != nil:
169			return RestoreResult{}, err
170		}
171	
172		// Resolve the change id: an ordinary row, a prior restore and a
173		// compacted-away id's retained summary are handled differently, so consult
174		// all three.
175		var existingCursor int64
176		var existingDevice string
177		var existingPayload []byte
178		err = tx.QueryRow(
179			`SELECT cursor, device_id, payload FROM changes WHERE document_id = ? AND id = ?`,
180			documentID, changeID,
181		).Scan(&existingCursor, &existingDevice, &existingPayload)
182		switch {
183		case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
184			// No online row: the id may belong to a change compaction trimmed.
185			// Its retained summary still decides — an idempotent restore needs the
186			// same device, snapshot cursor and source state; an id left by an
187			// ordinary trimmed change is a conflict, as is any mismatch.
188			var summaryDevice string
189			var summaryDigest []byte
190			var summaryCursor int64
191			var restoredFrom sql.NullInt64
192			err := tx.QueryRow(
193				`SELECT device_id, digest, cursor, restored_from FROM change_identities
194				 WHERE document_id = ? AND id = ?`,
195				documentID, changeID,
196			).Scan(&summaryDevice, &summaryDigest, &summaryCursor, &restoredFrom)
197			switch {
198			case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
199				// Genuinely new id; fall through to append below.
200			case err != nil:
201				return RestoreResult{}, err
202			default:
203				stateDigest, err := payloadDigest(state)
204				if err != nil {
205					return RestoreResult{}, err
206				}
207				if !restoredFrom.Valid || restoredFrom.Int64 != snapshotCursor ||
208					summaryDevice != deviceID || !bytes.Equal(summaryDigest, stateDigest) {
209					return RestoreResult{}, &ErrRestoreConflict{ID: changeID}
210				}
211				return RestoreResult{
212					ID:           changeID,
213					Created:      false,
214					Cursor:       summaryCursor,
215					RestoredFrom: snapshotCursor,
216				}, nil
217			}
218		case err != nil:
219			return RestoreResult{}, err
220		default:
221			var restDevice string
222			var restSnapshotCursor int64
223			var restState []byte
224			err = tx.QueryRow(
225				`SELECT device_id, snapshot_cursor, state FROM restores WHERE document_id = ? AND change_id = ?`,
226				documentID, changeID,
227			).Scan(&restDevice, &restSnapshotCursor, &restState)
228			switch {
229			case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
230				// The id belongs to an ordinary change (or a batch/merge change),
231				// not a restore: never treat it as an idempotent restore.
232				return RestoreResult{}, &ErrRestoreConflict{ID: changeID}
233			case err != nil:
234				return RestoreResult{}, err
235			default:
236				if restDevice != deviceID || restSnapshotCursor != snapshotCursor || !store.JSONEqual(restState, state) {
237					return RestoreResult{}, &ErrRestoreConflict{ID: changeID}
238				}
239				return RestoreResult{
240					ID:           changeID,
241					Created:      false,
242					Cursor:       existingCursor,
243					RestoredFrom: snapshotCursor,
244				}, nil
245			}
246		}
247	
248		nextCursor, err := currentCursorTx(tx, documentID)
249		if err != nil {
250			return RestoreResult{}, err
251		}
252		nextCursor++
253		if _, err := tx.Exec(
254			`INSERT INTO changes (document_id, cursor, id, device_id, payload) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)`,
255			documentID, nextCursor, changeID, deviceID, state,
256		); err != nil {
257			return RestoreResult{}, err
258		}
259		if _, err := tx.Exec(
260			`INSERT INTO restores (document_id, change_id, device_id, snapshot_cursor, change_cursor, state)
261			 VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)`,
262			documentID, changeID, deviceID, snapshotCursor, nextCursor, state,
263		); err != nil {
264			return RestoreResult{}, err
265		}
266	
267		if err := tx.Commit(); err != nil {
268			return RestoreResult{}, err
269		}
270		s.notifyWaiters(documentID)
271		return RestoreResult{
272			ID:           changeID,
273			Created:      true,
274			Cursor:       nextCursor,
275			RestoredFrom: snapshotCursor,
276		}, nil
277	}

1	// Package events is the change event service: the durable per-document change
2	// log together with everything written on top of it.
3	//
4	// Within a document every change has a client-supplied id. New ids receive a
5	// monotonically increasing cursor; re-posting an existing id is idempotent
6	// only when the deviceId and decoded JSON payload match, otherwise it is a
7	// conflict. Valid batches commit atomically in one serialized transaction, so
8	// cursors never repeat and no record is partially written, even under
9	// concurrent writers. Ordinary posts, offline replays, merges and snapshot
10	// restores all allocate from the same per-document contiguous cursor space.
11	//
12	// A document may also carry snapshots: caller-supplied JSON states pinned to
13	// existing change cursors. Snapshots are write-once per cursor — a matching
14	// re-post is idempotent, a differing one a conflict — and live apart from the
15	// change log. A restore appends an ordinary change whose payload is a
16	// snapshot's state, recording its provenance so a repeated restore after a
17	// restart keeps the same idempotency/conflict decisions.
18	//
19	// Reads page by cursor in ascending order. The session view and the document
20	// view are the same read; the HTTP layer adds the session/permission checks.
21	// Long polling and push subscriptions are in-memory observers of commits:
22	// they register before the confirming read, hold no durable state, and are
23	// woken only after a change-bearing transaction has committed.
24	//
25	// The service owns only its own tables. The registration and permission
26	// layers are reached through its Gate interface, so a replay or merge never
27	// reaches into another service's storage.
28	package events
29	
30	import (
31		"encoding/json"
32		"errors"
33		"fmt"
34	)
35	
36	// ErrStoreClosing reports that the service is shutting down and parked long
37	// polls have been woken so they can return without writing anything. The
38	// caller maps it to 503.
39	var ErrStoreClosing = errors.New("store is closing")
40	
41	// Change is one element of an inbound batch or one row of a listing.
42	type Change struct {
43		ID       string          // client-supplied change id, unique per document
44		DeviceID string          // originating device
45		Payload  json.RawMessage // decoded JSON value, stored verbatim
46	}
47	
48	// Result reports the outcome for one element of an accepted batch.
49	type Result struct {
50		ID      string `json:"id"`
51		Created bool   `json:"created"`
52		Cursor  int64  `json:"cursor"`
53	}
54	
55	// ListedChange is one row in a ListChanges response.
56	type ListedChange struct {
57		ID       string          `json:"id"`
58		DeviceID string          `json:"deviceId"`
59		Payload  json.RawMessage `json:"payload"`
60		Cursor   int64           `json:"cursor"`
61	}
62	
63	// MergeResult reports the outcome of an accepted MergeChange. Outcome is one
64	// of "idempotent", "applied" or "merged".
65	type MergeResult struct {
66		ID      string  `json:"id"`
67		Outcome string  `json:"outcome"`
68		Cursor  int64   `json:"cursor"`
69		Result  *Result `json:"result,omitempty"`
70	}
71	
72	// ErrConflict reports that a batch references an existing change id with a
73	// different deviceId or payload. The whole batch is rejected.
74	type ErrConflict struct {
75		ID string
76	}
77	
78	func (e *ErrConflict) Error() string {
79		return fmt.Sprintf("conflicting change %q for document", e.ID)
80	}
81	
82	// ErrStaleCursor reports that a merge targets a base cursor for an unknown
83	// document, or a base cursor greater than the document's current cursor. The
84	// caller maps it to 400; nothing is written.
85	var ErrStaleCursor = errors.New("baseCursor is unknown or ahead of the current cursor")
86	
87	// ErrSnapshotBase reports that a snapshot targets an unknown document or a
88	// cursor that is not an existing change cursor of the document. The caller
89	// maps it to 400; nothing is written.
90	var ErrSnapshotBase = errors.New("snapshot cursor is not an existing cursor of the document")
91	
92	// ErrCompactedBase reports that a merge targets a base cursor below the
93	// document's compaction boundary: the changes it would be checked against
94	// have left the online log, so the conflict check cannot be completed. The
95	// caller maps it to 400; nothing is written.
96	var ErrCompactedBase = errors.New("baseCursor is below the compaction boundary")
97	
98	// ErrSnapshotNotFound reports that no snapshot exists for the document and
99	// cursor. The caller maps it to 404.
100	var ErrSnapshotNotFound = errors.New("snapshot not found")
101	
102	// ErrSnapshotConflict reports that a snapshot already exists for the document
103	// and cursor with a different state. The stored snapshot is left unchanged.
104	type ErrSnapshotConflict struct {
105		Cursor int64
106	}
107	
108	func (e *ErrSnapshotConflict) Error() string {
109		return fmt.Sprintf("conflicting snapshot for cursor %d", e.Cursor)
110	}
111	
112	// ErrRestoreConflict reports that a restore references a change id that is
113	// already taken by an ordinary change, or by a prior restore whose deviceId,
114	// snapshot cursor or source state differs. Nothing is written; the caller maps
115	// it to 409.
116	type ErrRestoreConflict struct {
117		ID string
118	}
119	
120	func (e *ErrRestoreConflict) Error() string {
121		return fmt.Sprintf("change id %q conflicts with the change log", e.ID)
122	}
123	
124	// ExportedSnapshot is one row of an ExportSnapshots result.
125	type ExportedSnapshot struct {
126		Cursor int64           `json:"cursor"`
127		State  json.RawMessage `json:"state"`
128	}
129	
130	// RestoreResult reports the outcome of an accepted RestoreSnapshot.
131	type RestoreResult struct {
132		ID           string `json:"id"`
133		Created      bool   `json:"created"`
134		Cursor       int64  `json:"cursor"`
135		RestoredFrom int64  `json:"restoredFrom"`
136	}
137	
138	// schema is created when the service is constructed. Table and index shapes
139	// are unchanged from the pre-refactor layout, so data already on disk stays
140	// readable.
141	const schema = `
142	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS changes (
143		document_id TEXT NOT NULL,
144		cursor      INTEGER NOT NULL,
145		id          TEXT NOT NULL,
146		device_id   TEXT NOT NULL,
147		payload     BLOB NOT NULL,
148		PRIMARY KEY (document_id, id)
149	);
150	CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS changes_doc_cursor_idx
151		ON changes(document_id, cursor);
152	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS snapshots (
153		document_id TEXT NOT NULL,
154		cursor      INTEGER NOT NULL,
155		state       BLOB NOT NULL,
156		PRIMARY KEY (document_id, cursor)
157	);
158	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS restores (
159		document_id     TEXT NOT NULL,
160		change_id       TEXT NOT NULL,
161		device_id       TEXT NOT NULL,
162		snapshot_cursor INTEGER NOT NULL,
163		change_cursor   INTEGER NOT NULL,
164		state           BLOB NOT NULL,
165		PRIMARY KEY (document_id, change_id)
166	);
167	CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS restores_doc_cursor_idx
168		ON restores(document_id, change_cursor);
169	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS change_boundaries (
170		document_id TEXT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
171		boundary    INTEGER NOT NULL
172	);
173	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS change_identities (
174		document_id   TEXT NOT NULL,
175		id            TEXT NOT NULL,
176		device_id     TEXT NOT NULL,
177		digest        BLOB NOT NULL,
178		cursor        INTEGER NOT NULL,
179		restored_from INTEGER,
180		PRIMARY KEY (document_id, id)
181	);
182	`

9	// DocumentExists reports whether documentID is a known document rather than an
10	// empty namespace: it has any online change row, or a compaction boundary from

12	func (s *Service) DocumentExists(documentID string) (bool, error) {
13		var known bool
14		if err := s.db.QueryRow(
15			`SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM changes WHERE document_id = ?)
16			 OR EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM change_boundaries WHERE document_id = ?)`,

24	// ListChanges returns at most limit changes for documentID whose cursor is
25	// greater than after and still online, in cursor order, together with the
26	// cursor to pass as the next after value. An unknown document yields an empty
27	// list and cursor 0; a known document with no rows past after yields
28	// nextCursor == max(after, boundary), so a caller positioned inside the
29	// trimmed range resumes from the compaction boundary.
30	func (s *Service) ListChanges(documentID string, after, limit int64) ([]ListedChange, int64, error) {
31		rows, err := s.db.Query(
32			`SELECT id, device_id, payload, cursor FROM changes

172			s.mu.Lock()
173			closing := s.closed
174			s.mu.Unlock()
175			if closing {

183			// nextCursor == after for an empty page.

192	// removal function. The channel is closed on the next committed change to the
193	// document, or when the service stops.
194	func (s *Service) registerWait(documentID string) (ch chan struct{}, remove func()) {
195		ch = make(chan struct{}, 1)
196	
197		s.mu.Lock()
198		defer s.mu.Unlock()
199		if s.closed {

208		if set == nil {

210			s.waits[documentID] = set
211		}
212		set[id] = ch
213		return ch, func() {
214			s.mu.Lock()
215			if set, ok := s.waits[documentID]; ok {
216				delete(set, id)
217				if len(set) == 0 {
218					delete(s.waits, documentID)

1	// Change-log compaction moves the old end of a document's change log out of
2	// the online tables without touching the cursor space the log shares with
3	// every write path.
4	//
5	// The compaction boundary is the greatest cursor that has a saved snapshot
6	// (zero when the document has none): everything at or below it is reproducible
7	// from a snapshot plus the surviving tail, so those rows leave the online log.
8	// A trimmed change is not forgotten, though — its id keeps a small canonical
9	// summary (the originating device, a digest of the payload and, for a restore,
10	// the snapshot it came from, plus the cursor it was first assigned) so the
11	// submission layer keeps answering idempotency and conflict exactly as before.
12	// The summary never participates in reads: pagination, long polling and
13	// subscriptions simply no longer see the trimmed rows, and the summary's
14	// fixed size means storage does not grow back to the pre-compaction shape.
15	//
16	// Compaction itself is not a change: it allocates no cursor, writes no change
17	// record and wakes no waiter or subscriber. The cursor space never resets —
18	// the next allocated cursor is one past the greater of the online maximum and
19	// the boundary — and the boundary, the summaries and the read results are
20	// durable across restarts.
21	
22	package events
23	
24	import (
25		"bytes"
26		"crypto/sha256"
27		"database/sql"
28		"encoding/json"
29		"errors"
30	
31		"github.com/alicegogogogogo/local-first-sync-service/internal/store"
32	)
33	
34	// CompactChanges moves every change of documentID whose cursor is at or below
35	// the compaction boundary out of the online log, in one serialized
36	// transaction, and returns the boundary together with the number of changes
37	// removed by this call.
38	//
39	// The boundary is the greatest cursor with a saved snapshot, or zero when the
40	// document has no snapshot — compacting a snapshot-less or unknown document
41	// succeeds and removes nothing. The gate is enforced before any content is
42	// observed, exactly as in ReplayChanges: an unregistered device yields
43	// store.ErrDeviceNotFound and a revoked device yields store.ErrPermissionDenied,
44	// and neither touches any state.
45	//
46	// Each trimmed id keeps its canonical summary (device, payload digest, restore
47	// provenance and first cursor) so re-posting it stays idempotent and a
48	// differing re-post stays a conflict. Compaction is idempotent: a repeat finds
49	// the same boundary, trims nothing and reports zero removed. It commits no
50	// change row, allocates no cursor and notifies no waiter or subscriber.
51	func (s *Service) CompactChanges(documentID, deviceID string) (boundary, removed int64, err error) {
52		tx, err := s.db.Begin()
53		if err != nil {
54			return 0, 0, err
55		}
56		defer func() { _ = tx.Rollback() }()
57	
58		// Registration and permission are enforced before any change content is
59		// observed, so a rejected compaction cannot reveal anything.
60		if s.gate != nil {
61			if err := s.gate.DeviceAuthorizedTx(tx, documentID, deviceID); err != nil {
62				return 0, 0, err
63			}
64		}
65	
66		// The boundary is the greatest cursor with a saved snapshot, 0 when the
67		// document has none (an unknown document included).
68		if err := tx.QueryRow(
69			`SELECT COALESCE(MAX(cursor), 0) FROM snapshots WHERE document_id = ?`,
70			documentID,
71		).Scan(&boundary); err != nil {
72			return 0, 0, err
73		}
74		stored, err := boundaryOfTx(tx, documentID)
75		if err != nil {
76			return 0, 0, err
77		}
78		if boundary <= stored {
79			// Nothing new to trim (a repeat compaction, or a snapshot-less
80			// document): report the standing boundary and remove nothing.
81			return stored, 0, tx.Commit()
82		}
83	
84		// Collect the rows leaving the online log before deleting them: each one
85		// first moves its canonical summary into the identity table.
86		type trimmed struct {
87			cursor  int64
88			id      string
89			device  string
90			payload []byte
91		}
92		rows, err := tx.Query(
93			`SELECT cursor, id, device_id, payload FROM changes
94			 WHERE document_id = ? AND cursor <= ?
95			 ORDER BY cursor ASC`,
96			documentID, boundary,
97		)
98		if err != nil {
99			return 0, 0, err
100		}
101		var dropping []trimmed
102		for rows.Next() {
103			var t trimmed
104			if err := rows.Scan(&t.cursor, &t.id, &t.device, &t.payload); err != nil {
105				_ = rows.Close()
106				return 0, 0, err
107			}
108			dropping = append(dropping, t)
109		}
110		if err := rows.Err(); err != nil {
111			_ = rows.Close()
112			return 0, 0, err
113		}
114		_ = rows.Close()
115	
116		for _, t := range dropping {
117			// A restored change also carries its provenance into the summary, so a
118			// repeated restore keeps its idempotency/conflict decision.
119			var restoredFrom sql.NullInt64
120			err := tx.QueryRow(
121				`SELECT snapshot_cursor FROM restores WHERE document_id = ? AND change_id = ?`,
122				documentID, t.id,
123			).Scan(&restoredFrom)
124			switch {
125			case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
126				restoredFrom = sql.NullInt64{}
127			case err != nil:
128				return 0, 0, err
129			}
130			digest, err := payloadDigest(t.payload)
131			if err != nil {
132				return 0, 0, err
133			}
134			if _, err := tx.Exec(
135				`INSERT OR IGNORE INTO change_identities
136					(document_id, id, device_id, digest, cursor, restored_from)
137				 VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)`,
138				documentID, t.id, t.device, digest, t.cursor, restoredFrom,
139			); err != nil {
140				return 0, 0, err
141			}
142		}
143	
144		if _, err := tx.Exec(
145			`DELETE FROM restores WHERE document_id = ? AND change_cursor <= ?`,
146			documentID, boundary,
147		); err != nil {
148			return 0, 0, err
149		}
150		if _, err := tx.Exec(
151			`DELETE FROM changes WHERE document_id = ? AND cursor <= ?`,
152			documentID, boundary,
153		); err != nil {
154			return 0, 0, err
155		}
156		if _, err := tx.Exec(
157			`INSERT INTO change_boundaries (document_id, boundary) VALUES (?, ?)
158			 ON CONFLICT (document_id) DO UPDATE SET boundary = excluded.boundary`,
159			documentID, boundary,
160		); err != nil {
161			return 0, 0, err
162		}
163	
164		if err := tx.Commit(); err != nil {
165			return 0, 0, err
166		}
167		// Compaction is not a change: no waiter is woken and no subscriber is
168		// signaled, because no new change exists to observe.
169		return boundary, int64(len(dropping)), nil
170	}
171	
172	// boundaryOfTx returns the stored compaction boundary of documentID, or zero
173	// when the document was never compacted.
174	func boundaryOfTx(q store.DBTX, documentID string) (int64, error) {
175		var boundary int64
176		err := q.QueryRow(
177			`SELECT boundary FROM change_boundaries WHERE document_id = ?`,
178			documentID,
179		).Scan(&boundary)
180		switch {
181		case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
182			return 0, nil
183		case err != nil:
184			return 0, err
185		default:
186			return boundary, nil
187		}
188	}
189	
190	// currentCursorTx returns the document's high-water mark: the greatest online
191	// cursor, or the compaction boundary when every change up to it has left the
192	// online log. The cursor space never resets, so a fully trimmed document
193	// continues from its boundary rather than from zero.
194	func currentCursorTx(tx *sql.Tx, documentID string) (int64, error) {
195		var maxOnline int64
196		if err := tx.QueryRow(
197			`SELECT COALESCE(MAX(cursor), 0) FROM changes WHERE document_id = ?`,
198			documentID,
199		).Scan(&maxOnline); err != nil {
200			return 0, err
201		}
202		boundary, err := boundaryOfTx(tx, documentID)
203		if err != nil {
204			return 0, err
205		}
206		if boundary > maxOnline {
207			maxOnline = boundary
208		}
209		return maxOnline, nil
210	}
211	
212	// payloadDigest renders a payload in the canonical form JSONEqual compares —
213	// the decoded value re-encoded, so 1 and 1.0 or reordered object keys digest
214	// alike — and hashes it. The digest is the fixed-size stand-in for the payload
215	// in a trimmed change's retained summary.
216	func payloadDigest(payload json.RawMessage) ([]byte, error) {
217		var v any
218		if err := json.Unmarshal(payload, &v); err != nil {
219			return nil, err
220		}
221		canonical, err := json.Marshal(v)
222		if err != nil {
223			return nil, err
224		}
225		sum := sha256.Sum256(canonical)
226		return sum[:], nil
227	}
228	
229	// resolveTrimmedIdentity answers the submission question for an id whose
230	// online row is absent because compaction trimmed it. It returns found=true
231	// and the id's first cursor when the retained summary matches the incoming
232	// device and payload (an idempotent re-post), an *ErrConflict when a retained
233	// summary exists but differs, and found=false when no summary was retained (a
234	// genuinely new id).
235	func resolveTrimmedIdentity(tx *sql.Tx, documentID string, c Change) (found bool, cursor int64, err error) {
236		var device string
237		var digest []byte
238		err = tx.QueryRow(
239			`SELECT device_id, digest, cursor FROM change_identities WHERE document_id = ? AND id = ?`,
240			documentID, c.ID,
241		).Scan(&device, &digest, &cursor)
242		switch {
243		case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
244			return false, 0, nil
245		case err != nil:
246			return false, 0, err
247		}
248	
249		incoming, err := payloadDigest(c.Payload)
250		if err != nil {
251			return false, 0, err
252		}
253		if device != c.DeviceID || !bytes.Equal(digest, incoming) {
254			return false, 0, &ErrConflict{ID: c.ID}
255		}
256		return true, cursor, nil
257	}

1	// Package authz is the permission service: the durable, per-document and
2	// per-device authorization ledger together with the system's single revoke
3	// verdict.
4	//
5	// Every (document, device) pair starts authorized; a grant or revoke is
6	// recorded per pair. The lookup and the write run in one serialized
7	// transaction on the shared connection and commit to disk, so concurrent
8	// grant/revoke calls each land as a complete state and survive a restart.
9	//
10	// The other services do not read the permission table. They take their
11	// registration-and-authorization verdict through AuthorizedTx, evaluated
12	// inside their own write transaction, so a rejected request is judged before
13	// any document content is observed and the gate and the gated work commit as
14	// one judgment. Revoking never deletes changes, snapshots, sessions or CRDT
15	// state; it only produces the denial and, after the revoke commits, notifies
16	// the registered revoke sinks (the live subscription registries) so they can
17	// end the affected connections with the one-time, sticky 4403 close.
18	package authz
19	
20	import (
21		"database/sql"
22		"errors"
23		"sync"
24	
25		"github.com/alicegogogogogo/local-first-sync-service/internal/store"
26	)
27	
28	// schema is created when the service is constructed; its shape is unchanged
29	// from the pre-refactor layout, so authorization rows already on disk stay
30	// readable.
31	const schema = `
32	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS document_permissions (
33		document_id TEXT NOT NULL,
34		device_id   TEXT NOT NULL,
35		authorized  INTEGER NOT NULL,
36		PRIMARY KEY (document_id, device_id)
37	);
38	`
39	
40	// RevokeSink observes a committed revoke. The change event service and the
41	// CRDT service register themselves to end the affected live subscriptions; a
42	// sink must not block and must be safe to call after the revoke transaction
43	// has committed. The permission service depends on this interface alone, so
44	// the dependency points from the observers toward the verdict and never back.
45	type RevokeSink interface {
46		PermissionRevoked(documentID, deviceID string)
47	}
48	
49	// Service is the permission service.
50	type Service struct {
51		db *sql.DB
52	
53		mu    sync.Mutex
54		sinks []RevokeSink
55	}
56	
57	// New constructs the permission service over the shared kernel handle and
58	// creates its table.
59	func New(kernel *store.Store) (*Service, error) {
60		db := kernel.DB()
61		if _, err := db.Exec(schema); err != nil {
62			return nil, err
63		}
64		return &Service{db: db}, nil
65	}
66	
67	// AddRevokeSink registers an observer notified after every committed revoke.
68	// It is called by the composition root while wiring the services, before the
69	// surface serves requests.
70	func (s *Service) AddRevokeSink(sink RevokeSink) {
71		s.mu.Lock()
72		s.sinks = append(s.sinks, sink)
73		s.mu.Unlock()
74	}
75	
76	// AuthorizedTx is the shared gate: it returns nil when deviceID is registered
77	// and currently authorized for documentID, store.ErrDeviceNotFound when the
78	// device is not registered and store.ErrPermissionDenied when its access has
79	// been revoked. It runs inside the caller's transaction q, so the verdict is
80	// taken on the same serialized connection as the work it guards, before any
81	// document content is read.
82	func (s *Service) AuthorizedTx(q store.DBTX, documentID, deviceID string) error {
83		exists, err := store.DeviceExistsTx(q, deviceID)
84		if err != nil {
85			return err
86		}
87		if !exists {
88			return store.ErrDeviceNotFound
89		}
90		var stored int
91		err = q.QueryRow(
92			`SELECT authorized FROM document_permissions WHERE document_id = ? AND device_id = ?`,
93			documentID, deviceID,
94		).Scan(&stored)
95		switch {
96		case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
97			// No deviation row: devices start authorized.
98			return nil
99		case err != nil:
100			return err
101		default:
102			if stored == 0 {
103				return store.ErrPermissionDenied
104			}
105			return nil
106		}
107	}
108	
109	// DeviceAuthorizedTx adapts the shared gate to the change event and CRDT
110	// services' Gate interface (which names *sql.Tx). The verdict is identical.
111	func (s *Service) DeviceAuthorizedTx(tx *sql.Tx, documentID, deviceID string) error {
112		return s.AuthorizedTx(tx, documentID, deviceID)
113	}
114	
115	// SetDocumentPermission grants or revokes deviceID's access to documentID and
116	// reports whether the stored permission actually changed.
117	//
118	// Every device starts authorized for every document, so the first revoke is
119	// the first write for the pair (changed=true); repeating a state that already
120	// holds writes nothing and reports changed=false. An unregistered device
121	// yields store.ErrDeviceNotFound and nothing is written. The lookup and the
122	// write run in one serialized transaction, so concurrent grant/revoke calls
123	// each commit completely and the final state matches the last committed
124	// action. After a revoke commits, every registered sink is notified; a grant
125	// notifies nothing (a prior revoke already ended the connection stickily).
126	func (s *Service) SetDocumentPermission(documentID, deviceID string, authorized bool) (changed bool, err error) {
127		tx, err := s.db.Begin()
128		if err != nil {
129			return false, err
130		}
131		defer func() { _ = tx.Rollback() }()
132	
133		exists, err := store.DeviceExistsTx(tx, deviceID)
134		if err != nil {
135			return false, err
136		}
137		if !exists {
138			return false, store.ErrDeviceNotFound
139		}
140	
141		current := true // devices start authorized; a row only records a deviation
142		var stored int
143		err = tx.QueryRow(
144			`SELECT authorized FROM document_permissions WHERE document_id = ? AND device_id = ?`,
145			documentID, deviceID,
146		).Scan(&stored)
147		switch {
148		case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
149			// No row: the default (authorized) holds.
150		case err != nil:
151			return false, err
152		default:
153			current = stored != 0
154		}
155		if current == authorized {
156			return false, tx.Commit()
157		}
158	
159		v := 0
160		if authorized {
161			v = 1
162		}
163		if _, err := tx.Exec(
164			`INSERT INTO document_permissions (document_id, device_id, authorized) VALUES (?, ?, ?)
165			 ON CONFLICT (document_id, device_id) DO UPDATE SET authorized = excluded.authorized`,
166			documentID, deviceID, v,
167		); err != nil {
168			return false, err
169		}
170		if err := tx.Commit(); err != nil {
171			return false, err
172		}
173	
174		// A grant cannot unblock a subscription (the first revoke already ended
175		// it, stickily); only a revoke needs to end live subscriptions.
176		if !authorized {
177			s.mu.Lock()
178			sinks := append([]RevokeSink(nil), s.sinks...)
179			s.mu.Unlock()
180			for _, sink := range sinks {
181				sink.PermissionRevoked(documentID, deviceID)
182			}
183		}
184		return true, nil
185	}
186	
187	// DeleteDevicePermissionsTx removes every document-permission ledger row that
188	// names deviceID, inside the caller's transaction: grants and revokes the
189	// deregistered device held on documents vanish together with the device. It is
190	// the permission service's share of device deregistration, run in the same
191	// serialized transaction as the registration layer's cascade, so the row
192	// removals and the device deletion commit as one judgment. After the device
193	// row is gone the default verdict would be "unregistered" anyway; clearing the
194	// rows guarantees a device that later re-registers the same id starts with no
195	// inherited authorization state.
196	func (s *Service) DeleteDevicePermissionsTx(q store.DBTX, deviceID string) error {
197		_, err := q.Exec(
198			`DELETE FROM document_permissions WHERE device_id = ?`, deviceID,
199		)
200		return err
201	}
202	
203	// DocumentAuthorized reports whether deviceID currently holds permission for
204	// documentID. Devices start authorized, so an absent row means authorized.
205	func (s *Service) DocumentAuthorized(documentID, deviceID string) (bool, error) {
206		var stored int
207		err := s.db.QueryRow(
208			`SELECT authorized FROM document_permissions WHERE document_id = ? AND device_id = ?`,
209			documentID, deviceID,
210		).Scan(&stored)
211		switch {
212		case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
213			return true, nil
214		case err != nil:
215			return false, err
216		default:
217			return stored != 0, nil
218		}
219	}
220	
221	// PermissionEntry is one row of a document's permission ledger: a currently
222	// registered device id together with its authorization for the document.
223	type PermissionEntry struct {
224		DeviceID   string
225		Authorized bool
226	}
227	
228	// ListDocumentPermissions is the read-only ledger view of one document: one
229	// entry per currently registered device, in ascending lexicographic device-id
230	// order, paged by limit/offset against that same order.
231	//
232	// A device with no ledger row starts authorized, so its entry reports
233	// Authorized=true; a device whose latest committed action was a revoke reports
234	// false. Deregistered devices carry no device row and their ledger rows were
235	// removed by the deregistration cascade, so they never appear. An unknown
236	// document is indistinguishable from one on which every device keeps the
237	// default: every registered device lists authorized. The read runs in one
238	// serialized transaction, creates no row, moves no cursor and notifies no sink.
239	func (s *Service) ListDocumentPermissions(documentID string, limit, offset int64) ([]PermissionEntry, error) {
240		tx, err := s.db.Begin()
241		if err != nil {
242			return nil, err
243		}
244		defer func() { _ = tx.Rollback() }()
245	
246		rows, err := tx.Query(
247			`SELECT d.id, COALESCE(p.authorized, 1) AS authorized
248			 FROM devices d
249			 LEFT JOIN document_permissions p
250			   ON p.document_id = ? AND p.device_id = d.id
251			 ORDER BY d.id ASC
252			 LIMIT ? OFFSET ?`,
253			documentID, limit, offset,
254		)
255		if err != nil {
256			return nil, err
257		}
258		defer func() { _ = rows.Close() }()
259	
260		entries := make([]PermissionEntry, 0)
261		for rows.Next() {
262			var entry PermissionEntry
263			var stored int
264			if err := rows.Scan(&entry.DeviceID, &stored); err != nil {
265				return nil, err
266			}
267			entry.Authorized = stored != 0
268			entries = append(entries, entry)
269		}
270		if err := rows.Err(); err != nil {
271			return nil, err
272		}
273		return entries, tx.Commit()
274	}
